title: fix(sse): correct partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing for streaming API
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Context: Several customers and internal tests showed that SSE streaming responses could emit partial-JSON payloads with delimiters/events emitted out-of-order when tokenization boundaries aligned with framing boundaries. This caused the OpenAI-compatibility layer and some downstream SDKs to receive malformed partial JSONs or out-of-order token/event pairs, leading to structured-output consumers seeing temporary parse errors or incorrect final assembly.

Motivation: Fix the chunking/framing path to ensure deterministic ordering of delimiter markers, token events, and final partial-json close markers across the serving runtime and the OpenAI compatibility shim. This PR consolidates framing state, moves delimiter emission to a single responsibility in the SSE writer, and adds invariant checks to prevent reordering when batching or kv-cache flushes interleave with stream events.

What I changed (high level):
- Normalize SSE framing: introduce a single emit_delimiter() call in sse_writer used by all streaming code paths to guarantee ordering.
- Fix token/event ordering: ensure token events are always emitted before a partial-json delimiter close when a token finishes a JSON value.
- Partial-JSON handling: add a lightweight state machine in streaming/partial_json_state.go to track open/close delimiter counts and guard against duplicate closes when rerouting or failing over.
- OpenAI compat shim adjustments: update openai/shim_streaming.go to respect the new delimiter semantics and to coalesce event/meta messages so SDK consumers see consistent chunks.
- Tests: add deterministic unit tests and an integration test that fuzzes token boundaries to reproduce the original failure. Also added a harness test in perf-canary to validate across small and large batch sizes.

Testing/CI: Local unit and integration tests added. CI initially hit a flaky test in stream_reader_test (timeout) — reran the job and it passed. End-to-end streaming tests (integration) included to cover multi-chunk partial JSON assemblies.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Changes are backwards compatible at the wire level for well-formed streams; this PR tightens ordering so some malformed existing client behavior that tolerated reorderings will no longer silently accept bad sequences. We will monitor error rates and keep a short-lived fallback flag in runtime config for rapid rollback if necessary.

Related: ENG-4123 (streaming stability epic), SUP-88 (customer report: partial JSON parse errors).
